sentence: This project offers microscopy tools that take images of cells, tissues and organs inside a living animal over time.
This project studies how deleting a gene affects circuits between neurons and the function of the medial prefrontal cortex in Tuberous Sclerosis Complex.
This project tries to find signs of intestinal development that predict which very preterm infants will have feeding intolerance.
This project studies how tissue injury happens in patients with porphyrias, diseases caused by abnormal buildup of natural pigment byproducts.
This project uses a high-speed observation tool to study how the enzyme protein kinase A works normally and in mutant forms.
This project sets up standard vectors, virus preparations and cell cultures that many research projects can share.
This project supports basic cancer research in the laboratory and moves discoveries toward early pre-clinical development.
This project reviews earlier experiments on alcohol warning labels and runs more experiments to find what makes cancer warnings work better.
This project tries to find out where the dark proteome comes from and how it works in cancer.
This project measures how changing the dosage of craniofacial transcription factors affects cells and facial traits in disease.
This project builds a public resource that lists the regulatory switches in the human genome and the genes they control.
This project tries to find out which cells in the mouth and nose the virus affects and how it triggers an inflammatory response.
This project studies how endothelial dysfunction leads to atrial fibrillation.
This project develops a mass spectrometer that uses ion mobility spectrometry to read phosphorylation patterns on G-protein coupled membrane receptors.
This project develops drug discovery technology to find allosteric kinase inhibitors for use against cancer.
This project builds a tool that measures gene expression over time inside tissues, including inflammatory cytokines.
This project studies how a skeletal stem cell helps limbs regenerate after amputation.
This project studies how repeating sequences in DNA cause Fragile X diseases and looks for genes that modify these conditions.
This project develops image reconstruction algorithms that correct for heart motion so plaque activity in coronary arteries can be measured better.
This project tries to find changes in tumors and hosts that promote brain metastasis in breast cancer patients.
